about: The GITCRAFT style atlas: looks GITCRAFT can produce well with its own tools. A menu of what is possible, never a house style: a production's style shortlist is drawn from it to suit the product, and the person picks. Every look is rendered as the same two samples (scenes/atlas.json).

families.raster: raster treatment: pixels, grain, print textures (PhotoCraft, canvas)
families.type: typography leads: the look is mostly type, grid and rules
families.3d: real 3D models and renders (MeshCraft / Blender, Three.js)
families.shader: procedural canvas and shader work (light, glow, generated pattern)

looks.name: Flat Geometric
looks.suits: Bright casual games and friendly consumer apps that must read instantly at thumbnail size.
looks.hard: It goes bland fast: without one bold colour idea and a strong silhouette it looks like a template.

looks.name: Neon Vector
looks.suits: Fast arcade games, rhythm games and night-time music or nightlife apps.
looks.hard: Glow everywhere flattens hierarchy and costs legibility; small text needs a solid fill, and it fails in daylight.

tells.reason: in a neon look the light is the material: lines emit their own glow
violet and magenta are the look's own inks, chosen with it

looks.name: Pixel Art
looks.suits: Retro action, platformers, roguelikes and cosy games; playful utilities with a game wink.
looks.hard: Every sprite is hand-placed; animation frames and detailed characters take real pixel artistry we only approximate.

looks.name: Risograph Print
looks.suits: Indie games with a handmade feel, culture and events apps, small publishers and shops.
looks.hard: Overprints and grain must stay off the text; two or three inks limit what states and errors can use.

looks.name: Swiss Grid
looks.suits: Transit, data and reference apps; puzzle games where clarity is the pleasure.
looks.hard: It relies on perfect spacing and a strict grid; one sloppy margin shows, and it can feel cold.

tells.reason: one neutral grotesque throughout is the Swiss rule, chosen on purpose

looks.name: Terminal Phosphor
looks.suits: Developer tools, hacking or text-adventure games, and anything that wants to feel like a machine talking.
looks.hard: Characters are the only pixels: images, curves and fine motion are almost impossible, and density tires the eye.

tells.reason: one monospace face for everything is the terminal look itself
phosphor bloom is how a CRT draws text

looks.name: Blueprint
looks.suits: Building, engineering and physics games; planning, measuring and maker tools.
looks.hard: Everything is a thin line: hierarchy needs care, and fills, photos or colourful states break it.

looks.name: Low-Poly 3D
looks.suits: 3D games and playful scenes that need depth and light without detailed models.
looks.hard: Characters need modelling and rigging; we build blocky ones well and organic ones poorly, and the web build must stay light.

looks.name: Linocut Ink
looks.suits: Folk tales, nature and craft games; recipe, garden and bookish apps.
looks.hard: Carved texture is generated, not cut by hand; at small sizes it turns to noise, so the UI must stay plain.

looks.name: Isometric Diorama
looks.suits: Builders, puzzle and strategy games, and dashboards that show a place or a system.
looks.hard: Characters and text at an angle are awkward; it needs a strict 2:1 grid and careful draw order.

looks.name: Halftone Comic
looks.suits: Action, story and party games; social apps with a loud voice.
looks.hard: Busy dots fight small text, and drawing expressive characters is beyond us; it works with simple bold shapes.

looks.name: Editorial Serif
looks.suits: Story and word games, reading, food and travel apps that want to feel considered.
looks.hard: Needs real hierarchy and generous space; on small phones the big serif crowds the content.

looks.name: Topographic Map
looks.suits: Exploration and outdoor games; maps, hiking, weather and sailing apps.
looks.hard: Generated contours read as texture, not place, unless they follow real terrain; labels must never sit on lines.
tools: canvas (marching squares on a height field)

looks.name: Notebook Sketch
looks.suits: Casual and puzzle games, journals, study and planning apps.
looks.hard: The wobble is generated, not a real hand: a whole screen of it looks mechanical, and it can read as unfinished.

cannot.name: Painterly
cannot.why: Brush strokes with intent (where the light falls, what to leave out) need a painter or an image model; GITCRAFT has neither, and filters over shapes look like filters.

cannot.name: Photoreal
cannot.why: Believable materials, faces and light need scanned assets or a GPU render farm; MeshCraft renders stylised scenes, and photographs the person supplies can only be used, not made.

cannot.name: Detailed characters
cannot.why: Faces, hands and expressive poses need an artist or a modelled and rigged character; we build simple silhouettes and blocky models well and anatomy badly.

cannot.name: Frame-by-frame animation
cannot.why: Hand-drawn in-betweens (the bounce of a cartoon run cycle) are many drawings per second; we animate with transforms, tweens and procedural motion, and 3D clips through AnimCraft.

cannot.name: Anime / cel-shaded illustration
cannot.why: It is a drawing tradition: line confidence, faces and hair. Toon shaders on simple models are possible; the illustration style is not.
